findings.title: Fallback locales are only ensured loaded in web controllers
findings.body: `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` is only called from `ApplicationController#set_locale`. The translate accelerator's `I18n.translate` loads only `config.locale`, and `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` performs fallback lookups by calling the backend directly for the fallback locales, so it will not trigger loading of the default or English translation files. Any server-side translation done outside this controller before-filter (Sidekiq jobs, mailers, rake tasks, or `I18n.with_locale` blocks) will therefore not have the fallback locales loaded and missing translations will not fall back.

findings.title: Fallback chain can raise when SiteSetting/default locale is unavailable or blank
findings.body: `FallbackLocaleList#[]` calls `SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym` unconditionally. This method is invoked by I18n during fallback lookups, which can happen early in boot, in rake tasks, or when a translation is missing. If `SiteSetting.default_locale` is nil, blank, or SiteSetting is not ready, this raises instead of falling back (the subsequent `compact` cannot remove a nil because `to_sym` is called first). A missing translation can become an exception.

findings.title: Lazy initialization of @loaded_locales is not thread-safe
findings.body: `ensure_loaded!` initializes `@loaded_locales` with `||=` outside the existing `LOAD_MUTEX`, while `translate` reads `@loaded_locales` without a nil guard and `load_locale` mutates it under the mutex. In a multithreaded process, first-use races can overwrite the array or leave it uninitialized for a thread that calls `translate` first, causing duplicate locale loads or a NoMethodError on `@loaded_locales.include?`.

findings.title: Custom I18n.fallbacks object does not behave like the standard fallback object
findings.body: `I18n.fallbacks` is replaced with a `Hash` subclass that only overrides `[]` and adds `ensure_loaded!`. It returns a new array on every lookup, does not cache fallback chains, and ignores normal hash mutation/assignment. Code or plugins expecting the standard `I18n::Locale::Fallbacks` API (for example `defaults`, cached lookup results, or appending to `I18n.fallbacks[locale]`) will not work and may fail silently.
